name: GIS General Examples
miniText: How can geographic datasets become queryable agent and grid information without losing their spatial meaning? NetLogo GIS General Examples loads city points, river lines, country polygons, and an elevation raster, then demonstrates drawing, queries, projection choices, and conversion to turtles or patches. Westervelt [1] connects GIS with agent modeling, Parker and colleagues [2] review spatial land-change simulation, and Crooks and colleagues [3] discuss geospatial modeling challenges. These sources motivate the integration problem rather than treating a successful map import as a scientific model. Coordinate reference systems, projection, resolution, geometry type, and data coverage are essential assumptions. Drawing layers are representations, while converted agent or patch attributes can become inputs to later rules. The baseline illustrates geospatial interoperability; it does not itself explain urban growth, establish dataset accuracy, or validate a subsequent agent-based application.
